newsitem.title: KENYA: Heavy inflows sustain Kenya shilling bull vs dlr.
newsitem.headline: Heavy inflows sustain Kenya shilling bull vs dlr.

text.p: The Kenyan shilling gained against the dollar on Tuesday, boosted by heavy dollar inflows from the agricultural sector, commercial bank dealers said.
The Central Bank of Kenya posted a shilling mean rate of 54.78 against the dollar from 54.85 on Monday, while against the pound, it was posted at a mean rate of 88.63 from 87.96.
"There were very few buyers in the market as most traders opted to wait in the face of a strengthening shilling," one dealer said.
Dealers said the shilling looked set to strengthen in the short term because of a lack of demand amid increasing inflows from foreign investors looking to buy treasury bills.
"The market fundamentals appear to favour a strong shilling," another dealer said.
The money market was was slightly tight with overnight rates quoted between 14 and 17 percent compared to 15-20 percent on Monday.
